sections.html:
Deeds for Oceana County property are filed with the Register of Deeds, whose office is inside the Hart courthouse. Reach it at (231) 873-4158 or write to P.O. Box 111, Hart, MI 49420. Voters elect the register to a four-year term, and the post makes that person the official keeper of the county's land records.

Behind the counter sits an index of everything recorded, plus the original plats for each subdivision. Local governments call on the office for liber and page numbers, instrument numbers and parcel descriptions taken from those plats. UCC financing statements may be filed there as well, and the register chairs the County Plat Board that signs off on new subdivisions.

You can request copies or file a document in person or by post, as long as the fee is enclosed. Include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Adding a daytime phone number lets staff call about a defect instead of returning the paper. The department page also links an online official records search.

sections.h2: Oceana County at a glance for sellers
sections.html:
Oceana is a rural West Michigan county on the Lake Michigan shore. Hart is the county seat and the largest incorporated community. The county has 27,177 people, 16,115 housing units and 10,419 households, and owners hold 84.5% of them. The typical owned home is worth $190,100, median rent is $759 a month, and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,280.

Prices here sit far below the Detroit suburbs, so the dollar cost of transfer tax and other percentage-based charges is lower even though the rates match. Only 136 building permits were issued during 2025, which tells you new construction is not flooding the market.

Recording and transfer tax stamps belong to the county that holds the parcel. Mason, Lake, Newaygo and Muskegon counties adjoin Oceana on land, so make sure the property lies in Oceana before you send a deed here. US 31 follows the western side through Hart and Pentwater, and M-20 crosses the south toward Hesperia.

State law, at MCL 600.2567, fixes recording at $30 for any document regardless of length. A charter county may set a different schedule by ordinance, so phone the Oceana office for the price list before you mail a check.

Fees a Michigan register of deeds may charge
ServiceAmount
Record one document$30.00
Each extra instrument covered by an assignment or discharge$3.00
Page of a copy$1.00
Certification of a recorded document$5.00
Grantor/grantee search, each year covered$0.50, with a $5.00 floor
Filing or looking up any other paper$1.00

Pay when you hand over the document. Electronic submissions have one business day after receipt, and the statute gives government agencies and tax foreclosure filings separate payment schedules.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a sale?
sections.html:
Two Michigan acts tax a deed's value: MCL 207.505 covers the county share and MCL 207.526 the state share. Transfers worth $100 or more owe both. The county takes 55 cents per $500 block and the state takes $3.75 per block, and any partial block counts as a full one. The seller or grantor is the taxpayer, so plan for it on your side of the closing statement.

The fraction rule matters on odd prices. A price that ends a little past a $500 mark still pays for the whole next block. Swapping two properties triggers tax on each deed, measured by the true value of what each deed conveys.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit alongside it.
  • The affidavit costs nothing to file, but the deed must say it is being filed.
  • Write any exemption you claim on the instrument.
  • A parcel lying in two counties pays each county on its share of the price.

Oceana's register posts a recording checklist drawn from MCL 565.201 and nearby sections. Miss one item and the paper comes back unrecorded, which can push a closing date, so run through it before anyone signs.

  • Signatures are originals, and typed, stamped or printed names appear below them.
  • Notary names match the signature names exactly.
  • A grantee address, by street or post office box, appears on each deed or assignment.
  • The drafter's name and address are on the document.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledges anything that conveys or burdens real estate.
  • A survivor clause needs a certified death certificate or other proof of death.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the court clerk.

The page layout has its own checks. Keep the top 2.5 inches of the first sheet blank and half an inch clear on every other edge. Print in black on white stock that weighs 20 pounds or more, in type of 10 points or larger, and use sheets between letter and legal size. The first line of print must name the recordable event in a single statement.

Oceana County accepts e-recording through Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or Indecomm Global Services. Sign up with one provider to begin. The register answers e-recording questions at (231) 873-4158.

E-recording is usually the quickest route for a house sale, since the title company submits the deed from its own office and the county never handles a paper original. Ask your closing agent at the start which provider they use, and whether the transfer tax is paid through the same submission.

A title company closing your sale can tell you whether it files through one of these services. For a family transfer or a paper deed, deliver the original to the courthouse or mail it with the fee and a return envelope.

sections.h2: Getting a deed recorded step by step
sections.html:
For a typical sale the title company handles everything, and you only sign. If you are doing a family transfer or a sale without a title company, the path is short.

  • Confirm the parcel lies in Oceana County.
  • Check the deed against the format rules above, including the blank top margin and the grantee address.
  • Put the full price on the deed, or attach the valuation affidavit.
  • Enclose the recording fee and the transfer tax, with a stamped return envelope.
  • Add a daytime phone number so staff can call if something needs fixing.

A cash buyer needs the same recording and pays the same fees. The deed still has to meet every formatting point, and the transfer tax still falls on the seller. Calling the office before you mail anything is the cheapest way to avoid a returned document. Keep copies of what you send, and keep the recorded original when it comes back, since it is your proof that title passed to the buyer.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Oceana County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: (231) 873-4158. The office sits in the Hart courthouse, and the post office box is 111, Hart, MI 49420.

faqs.q: Will the register accept a deed sent by post?
faqs.a: Yes, with enough fees enclosed. Add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, and a phone number so staff can resolve any question about the paperwork.

faqs.q: What does recording one document cost in Oceana County?
faqs.a: State law sets $30 per document, whatever the page count. Because a county schedule can differ, confirm the figure with the office before you send payment.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to file the transfer valuation affidavit?
faqs.a: No. The deed has to state that the affidavit is being filed, and the affidavit has to disclose the total consideration.

faqs.q: Who owes the Michigan transfer tax when an Oceana County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor does. The county levy is 55 cents and the state levy is $3.75, each applied to every $500 of value.
